written_from: IBM z/OS MVS JCL Reference (SA23-1385): the IF/THEN/ELSE/ENDIF statement construct (relational-expression keywords RC, ABEND, ABENDCC, RUN, the NOT / not-sign operators, nesting) and the EXEC COND parameter (EVEN, ONLY). Expected answers were written before jcl_flow ran on them. Page numbers are not cited: the manual was read by section and the sections are named in each basis.
scenario_input: given: per step that starts, {rc: n} (0-4095) or {abend: code}. A step with no entry in given does not start.
scenario_answer: expect: per step, run (started, whether it ended with an RC or abended) or bypass (did not start).

scenarios.basis: IF statement, THEN / ELSE clauses: outer 0 <= 4 true, so N3 runs and the nested IF (N3.RC = 0) true runs N4; its ELSE (N5) and the outer ELSE (N6) do not. N7: NOT (N2.RC = 0) false and N3.RUN = FALSE false (N3 ran). N8: N2.RC NG 4 (not greater than 4) true.
Nested IF false (4 = 0), so its ELSE clause N5 runs and its THEN clause N4 does not; the outer THEN clause was entered, the outer ELSE (N6) was not. N7 and N8 as nest-all-zero.

Outer IF false (8 <= 4): the outer ELSE clause N6 runs; N3 and both clauses of the nested IF, which lies inside the unselected THEN clause, do not run (the nested IF is not evaluated, so neither of its clauses is selected). N7: NOT (N2.RC = 0) false, but N3.RUN = FALSE is true (RUN page: the step did not start), so N7 runs. N8 true.
N7: NOT (12 = 0) true, runs (the NOT / not-sign operator reverses the relation). N8: 12 NG 4 false, bypass.

ASSUMED A3: after an abend an IF whose expression names neither ABEND nor ABENDCC starts nothing (the IF pages say this only for cancel, time-expiry and scheduling abends; the EXEC COND page says following steps are bypassed). Every later IF here is of that kind.

ABEND page: ABEND = TRUE is true only if some step abended; no step did, so the ELSE clause (A4) runs and A7 (ABEND = FALSE) runs. ABENDCC tests name no abend code: false. A8 COND=EVEN: nothing abended and no test coded, runs. A9 COND=ONLY: nothing abended, bypass.

ABEND = TRUE true: A3 runs although a step abended (an IF naming ABEND is evaluated after an abend), the ELSE clause does not. ABENDCC page: A2.ABENDCC = S0C7 true, A5 runs. A6: A2's code is not U0100 and A1 did not abend, false. A7 ABEND = FALSE false. EVEN runs after an abend; ONLY runs because a preceding step abended.

A2 carries no EVEN / ONLY and no IF: bypassed after the abend (EXEC COND page). A5: A2 did not execute, so a relational expression naming it is false (IBM relational-expression rule). A6: A2 did not execute, and A1 abended U0100, not S806: false.
As abn-a1-u0100, but A1.ABENDCC = S806 is true, and OR needs one true relation: A6 runs although A2.ABENDCC = U0100 is false.
An abend inside an ELSE clause. A5 and A6 name ABENDCC so they are evaluated: A2 did not abend, so A2.ABENDCC = S0C7 is false; A6 false. A7: ABEND = FALSE is now false. EVEN and ONLY as abn-a2-s0c7.

An IF clause around EXEC PROC: the procedure step runs as a whole when (B1.RC = 0) is true. ASSUMED A5: the step that calls a procedure is one step, with the highest return code of its procedure steps as its RC, and B2.RUN = TRUE is true when it started (the manual's RUN and RC pages define stepname.procstepname forms; a bare calling-step name is not stated). B3: RUN true and RC (highest so far, 0) < 8. B4 EVEN: runs.
(B1.RC = 0) false: the procedure step is bypassed. B3: B2.RUN = TRUE is false (B2 did not start). B4: EVEN, nothing abended, runs.
B3: B2.RUN = TRUE true, but RC is the highest return code so far (8) and 8 < 8 is false; the AND needs both. Assumption A5.
A3: after the abend the IF for B3 names no ABEND test, so B3 does not start. B4 COND=EVEN runs after an abend (EXEC COND page) in the same job as the IF clauses.

Parentheses group an AND inside an OR: (0 = 0 & 0 = 0) true, C3 runs. C4: RC (highest so far, 0) NL 8 (not less than 8) false. C6: C2.RC NE 0 false and C2.ABEND = TRUE false. C5 COND=(8,LE) tests every earlier step: 8 <= 0 false, runs. C7 COND=ONLY: nothing abended, bypass.
C3: the grouped AND is false (C1.RC = 4) but C1.RC = 4 is true, so the OR is true. C4: highest RC 4, 4 NL 8 false. C5: 8 <= 4 false, 8 <= 0 false, runs.
C3: (0 = 0 & 8 = 0) false, C1.RC = 4 false: bypass. C4: highest RC 8, 8 NL 8 true, runs. C6: C2.RC NE 0 true. C5: 8 <= 8 true for C2, bypass.

C3 and C4 name no ABEND test: not started after the abend (A3). C6 names C2.ABEND = TRUE, true, so the OR is true whatever C2.RC means for an abended step (ASSUMED A6: an abended step has no RC to compare, a relation on it is false; this expression does not depend on it). C5: no EVEN / ONLY, bypassed after an abend. C7 COND=ONLY: a preceding step abended, runs.

assumed.text: After an ordinary abend an IF whose expression does not name ABEND, ABENDCC or the negated ABEND does not start its step; carried over from tests/equivalence/jcl/fixture (the IF pages say it for cancel, time expiry and scheduling abends only).

A step that calls a procedure (EXEC PROC=) is one step for IF tests by its calling stepname: RC is the highest return code of its procedure steps, RUN is true when it started. The manual defines stepname.procstepname.RC; the bare calling-step form is not stated.
A relation on the RC of a step that abended is false (no return code exists). The manual is silent; no scenario depends on it.

refused.construct: stepname.procstepname.RC / .RUN / .ABEND on a step inside a procedure
refused.reason: documented by IBM, but the evaluator carries a procedure call as one step with no inner step rows; slice 2 (PROC resolution) owns it

refused.construct: a bare ABEND or RUN keyword with no relational operator
refused.reason: IBM requires the = TRUE / = FALSE form for these keywords; the bare form is not valid

refused.construct: ABENDCC compared with > < or a numeric range
refused.reason: IBM defines = and NE for ABENDCC only

refused.construct: AND and OR mixed in one IF without parentheses
refused.reason: IBM gives AND and OR one priority and no rule for mixing them (as in tests/equivalence/jcl/fixture)

refused.construct: IF with the not sign written as a glyph
refused.reason: NOT and the not sign are interchangeable in IBM's text; the fixture uses NOT because the sign is a code-page byte
